You are a meme-literate designer and comedy writer who makes phone wallpapers and printable calendars. Produce the complete content and design spec for "November 2026: Do You Understand Yet?", a pack of daily lock-screen calendar wallpapers starring an original cartoon polar bear, plus a printable desk calendar.

BUYER AND JOB
Teens and young adults in the US who follow the "Remember November 2026" meme on TikTok and Reels: a "meme from the future" whose joke is anticipation with no event at the end. The pack's job: let them be in on the joke on their lock screen every day of the month the meme points to, with a fresh deadpan line each day.

VERIFIED CALENDAR FACTS (use exactly)
November 2026 has 30 days. Nov 1 is a Sunday; Nov 30 is a Monday. Sunday-first grid: row 1 = 1-7, row 2 = 8-14, row 3 = 15-21, row 4 = 22-28, row 5 = 29-30. Thanksgiving is Thursday, Nov 26.

DELIVERABLE SPEC
1. 30 daily captions, one per date, each 40 characters or fewer, deadpan and escalating: early days "it's here, act normal", mid-month confusion, late-month acceptance, a shrug on Nov 30. Add 10 spare captions.
2. 30 daily lock screens. Master canvas 1290 x 2796 px; also 1179 x 2556 px and 1080 x 2400 px versions. Safe zones: keep the top 30% clear for the clock and the bottom 12% clear for buttons. Layout between 32% and 86% of the height: title "NOVEMBER 2026", the full month grid with that day circled, the day's caption, the bear in a corner pose.
3. 3 bonus wallpapers (no grid): bear balanced on its front paws ("do you understand yet?"), bear holding a wall calendar ("it's november."), bear shrugging next to a "30" page ("i still don't get it").
4. Printable desk calendar: US Letter landscape (11 x 8.5 in) and A4 landscape (297 x 210 mm), month grid with every caption in its date cell, bear at the top, 0.4 in margins.
5. A short "how to set your wallpaper" note (generic phone steps, no brand names).

Bear character (original; must look nothing like the viral AI image): flat 2D cartoon, round chunky body, thick rounded outlines, small dot eyes, tiny mint scarf, never photorealistic.
Fonts: Fredoka (headings) and Nunito (captions), free for commercial use. Palette: Arctic Night #0E1A2B (background), Snow #F4F7FA (text, bear), Ice Blue #A9D6E5 (grid lines), Glacier #5FA8D3 (accents), Signal Yellow #FFD23F (today circle), Scarf Mint #7ED3B2.

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS
- Original wording only. Deadpan, absurd, teen-safe: no profanity, no insults, no references to real people, news, tragedies or politics. Nov 3, 2026 is a US election day: write nothing political for any date. Keep Nov 11 respectful (no veterans jokes). Reading level: grade 5-7.
- Accuracy: every caption's weekday matches the facts above; every caption fits in 40 characters; nothing claims a real event will happen.

DIFFERENTIATION
Competitors print copies of the AI bear on shirts with the "is coming" framing that goes stale on Nov 1. This pack uses the calendar payoff, gives a new joke every day of November, uses original art and is instant digital, so there is no shipping lag on a hard-dated joke.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not describe, trace or recreate the viral AI polar-bear image or video frames.
- No musician names, song titles, lyrics or melodies; do not use the phrase "life goes on" anywhere.
- No brand names or trademarks.

OUTPUT FORMAT
1. Caption table: Date | Weekday | Caption | Character count, then the 10 spares.
2. A CSV block for Canva Bulk Create (columns: date, weekday, caption, grid_row, grid_col), with grid_col 1 = Sunday.
3. Lock-screen layout spec with pixel positions for the 1290 x 2796 master.
4. Bonus wallpaper text and poses.
5. Desk calendar layout for Letter and A4.
6. How-to note.
7. A ticked self-check: 30 captions, all 40 characters or fewer; weekdays and grid positions match (Nov 1 = Sunday, row 1 col 1; Nov 30 = Monday, row 5 col 2); nothing political or about real people; no song, musician or "life goes on"; bear described as an original flat cartoon.

- Version B caption: "Remember November 2026 - I still don't get it"
- Also write 10 alternate captions of 6 words or fewer that work after Nov 1, ranked by how quickly they read on a laptop lid.

- Bear (original; must look nothing like the viral AI image): flat 2D cartoon, round chunky body, thick rounded outlines, dot eyes, tiny mint scarf; no photorealism, no fur texture.
- Cut border: a solid Snow white offset of 0.125 in (about 38 px at 300 DPI) around the whole silhouette, with no thin spikes or gaps narrower than 0.0625 in.
- Sizes and files: 3 x 3 in (900 x 900 px), 4 x 4 in (1200 x 1200 px), 5.5 x 5.5 in (1650 x 1650 px) at 300 DPI, transparent PNG; plus a 3000 x 3000 px transparent master for single-sticker marketplaces.
- Readability: caption readable at the 3 in size from about 1 m; minimum cap height 0.15 in at 3 in.

STYLE
Palette: Snow #F4F7FA (bear body, border), Arctic Night #0E1A2B (outlines, caption text), Ice Blue #A9D6E5 (shading), Signal Yellow #FFD23F (banner fill), Scarf Mint #7ED3B2. Font: Fredoka Bold for the caption (free for commercial use), with Nunito ExtraBold as a fallback. Give exact sizes, line breaks, letter case and stroke weights.

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS
- Original wording; deadpan tone; no profanity; nothing political (Nov 3, 2026 is a US election day) and no references to real people or events. Reading level: grade 3-5.
- Accuracy: spell "November 2026" identically in both versions; confirm all files are square, 300 DPI and transparent, and the border is continuous.

DIFFERENTIATION
Competitors copy the AI bear onto apparel with "is coming" text. This uses original art and the after-the-fact punchline, and it matches the "Do You Understand Yet?" wallpaper bear so the two can be bundled.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not describe, trace or recreate the viral AI polar-bear image or video frames.
- No musician names, song titles, lyrics or melodies; never use the phrase "life goes on".
- No trademarks or brand names.

OUTPUT FORMAT
1. Layer-by-layer spec for Version A and Version B (bear, banner, text, border) with sizes and hex colors.
2. Export list (file names and pixel sizes).
3. The 10 ranked alternates.
4. Canva build steps (7 or fewer), including how to add the white offset border.
5. A ticked self-check: both captions exact; bear is an original flat cartoon; continuous 0.125 in border; files square, 300 DPI, transparent; nothing political; no song, musician or brand.
